items.statement: Adults entering the pharmacist-led pathway will reduce their daily opioid dose by a mean of at least 25 percent at 6 months, with pain interference no worse than at entry.
items.rationale: Need is high because the post depends on the answer; novelty is modest; feasibility is high because data come from existing calls.
items.risks: Dose falls for reasons other than the pathway; missing data among those who leave.

items.statement: Patients living more than 60 km away or needing an interpreter will disengage more often than other patients.
items.rationale: Replicates a pattern from a regional service and would change how support is offered.
items.risks: About 20 disengagement events limit the analysis to two predictors.

items.statement: Emergency visits for withdrawal or overdose will not rise during the first three months of the taper.
items.rationale: A safety question that the pathway must answer for the hospital.
items.risks: Events are rare; the study can only describe them.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected as the primary descriptive aim, h2 and h3 kept as secondary and safety aims.
